statement: policy_ingest's backed-rule catalog (crates/enforcer-security/src/policy_ingest/backing.rs, BackedRuleCatalog::track_h_snapshot) is a deliberately standalone id-list snapshot, not a live read of crate::rules::registry::build_all. registry.rs is part of the arc-19 skeleton's shared owns: set (every h01-h11 feature pack extends it), and h08's owns: set is disjoint by file from it; importing registry::build_all directly would make policy_ingest's ownership straddle a file it does not own.
why: h08's Parallel Ownership Notes explicitly forbid editing the arc-19 crate skeleton or its shared registry seam; the workpack only grants src/policy_ingest.rs + src/policy_ingest/** + the profile + its own tests/fixtures.
howToApply: When a new module needs to know which RuleIds have real Validator backing but does not own the registry file, keep an explicit synced snapshot list at construction time (documented as 'kept in sync by convention, reviewed together') rather than importing the registry module cross-boundary. Whoever next adds a Track H validator row to registry.rs should also add its id to BackedRuleCatalog::track_h_snapshot.

statement: thiserror derive enums must never name a field `source` unless it is genuinely meant to satisfy the std::error::Error::source() chain (a value implementing std::error::Error). Naming a plain String field `source` on a #[derive(thiserror::Error)] variant makes thiserror auto-infer it as the error-chain source field, producing a confusing E0599 'as_dyn_error' trait-bound error at compile time that does not obviously point at the real cause.
why: crates/enforcer-security/src/policy_ingest/error.rs originally had `source: String` (meaning: which input document) on three PolicyIngestError variants; cargo build failed with `String: StdError` not satisfied, which reads like an unrelated trait issue until you know thiserror's #[source]-by-name convention.
howToApply: When defining a thiserror enum, never use the bare word `source` as a struct field name for anything other than an actual chained error value; use a qualified name like `spec_source` or `input_source` instead, and reserve `source`/`#[source]` for a genuine `Box<dyn Error>`/concrete-error field.

statement: The h08 POLICY-SPEC-INGESTION honesty seam is implemented as: MechanizedProfile carries EVERY asserted rule (both backed and unbacked) as a ProfileRuleRowWire{ruleId,tier,backed}, and map_to_profile additionally emits one Finding (Severity::Warning) per unbacked rule whose detail names the rule id, its asserted tier, and points at `enforcer rule new <id>` (d01) as the fix. Nothing is silently dropped or silently promoted to backed:true.
why: The workpack's core requirement is that an asserted-but-unbacked rule must be visibly un-enforced, never fake-green; keeping the row in the profile (with backed:false) rather than omitting it lets a UI/consumer see the gap explicitly instead of it disappearing.
howToApply: Any future ingestion-style mapper (spec text -> mechanized artifact) in this codebase should follow the same pattern: keep unmechanized assertions visible in the output artifact with an explicit unbacked/unenabled flag, plus a separate structured Finding/flag record for the mechanization backlog (d01/d08), rather than filtering them out of the artifact entirely.
